Interface BodyElements<T>

Type Parameters:
T - The type of an element
All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
public interface BodyElements<T> extends AutoCloseable
The elements of a body, decoded one at a time as they are asked for, like a cursor: a JSON array or a JSON stream read with AsyncRequestBody.elements(Class). Nothing is read ahead of the caller: the next element is received and decoded when next() is called, or when the stage the forEach(Function) consumer returned for the previous element completes. 
request.elements(Person.class)
    .forEach(person -> people.saveAsync(person))
    .thenApply(done -> HttpResponse.accepted());

One operation at a time: an operation started while another one is in progress throws an IllegalStateException, at once, instead of returning a stage. The end of the body and closing are different: at the end of the body, next() completes with an empty optional and forEach(Function) completes normally, while closing during an operation completes that operation with a CancellationException, and an operation started after closing throws an IllegalStateException. Closing discards the rest of the body; the elements are closed when the method that read them completed, see AsyncRequestBody.

The stages complete on a thread chosen by the server, usually an I/O thread: a consumer must not block.

5.3.0
